people.name: Daniel Hufnagel
people.short_bio: Daniel Hufnagel, PhD, is an Assistant Professor of Neuroscience at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai. His research integrates behavioral neuroscience, molecular and cellular biology, multiomics, and computational approaches to investigate the mechanisms underlying individual vulnerability and resilience to psychiatric disorders, with a particular focus on alcohol use disorder.
people.research: Investigating the molecular mechanisms underlying individual vulnerability and resilience in psychiatric disorders.

people.name: Bruna Rattis
people.short_bio: Bruna Rattis, PhD, is a Brazilian researcher with a background in biotechnology, immunology, and experimental pathology. Her research interests focus on neuroimmunology, particularly the interactions between the nervous and immune systems in health and disease.
people.bio: Hi there! I’m Bruna Rattis, a Brazilian researcher with a background in biotechnology and a strong interest in immunology and experimental pathology. I hold a PhD in Sciences from the University of São Paulo (USP) and a master’s degree in Tropical Medicine and Public Health from the Federal University of Goiás (UFG), Brazil. My research interests include immunopathology, infectious diseases, neuroscience, and neuroimmune interactions, particularly the communication between the nervous and immune systems. At Mount Sinai, I’m excited to expand my research into neuroimmunology and explore the connections between these fields.

news.title: Hufnagel Lab
news.description: The Hufnagel Lab is officially opening its doors! We are excited to welcome new collaborations and work together to uncover the molecular and neural mechanisms underlying vulnerability and resilience to psychiatric disorders.
